title: Museums in Japan Host 'Plushie Sleepovers'
paragraphs: Many children love their stuffed animals and take them everywhere. In Japan, some museums are now inviting these soft toys to spend a few nights away from home on special "plushie sleepovers."

One of the best-known events is held at the National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo, which is also known as MOMAT. In 2026, the museum held its "Plushie Sleepover" from October 2 to October 18. Children from the age of one up to junior high school age could apply to send one stuffed animal. The toys had to be between 10 and 100 centimeters tall, and any kind of plushie was welcome, including popular characters.
There were only 20 places, so if too many children applied, the plushies were chosen by lottery. For past events, the number of applications has regularly reached around 1,000.

Families whose plushies were chosen brought them to the museum at the start of the event. Then the plushies became special guests. They visited the museum's collection galleries, where a professional photographer took pictures of them with paintings and sculptures. They also spent time in different parts of the museum and stayed there overnight.

After the event, the photos were made into an album and mailed to the children. The fee for taking part was 1,500 yen, which covered the album and the cost of sending it. The program is supported by the Adobe Foundation, and it aims to give children more chances to enjoy museums and art.

MOMAT is not the only place in Japan to offer this kind of experience. In August 2024, the Yumenoshima Tropical Plant Museum in Tokyo held a three-day, two-night "tour" for up to 10 plushies at a time. The toys relaxed in the museum's botanical garden during the summer holidays and returned home with an album and souvenirs.
For many children, seeing photos of a favorite toy enjoying an adventure can be a fun way to become interested in museums.
